title: Contenedores y reproducibilidad operativa
scope: FULL_SECTION_BASE: live card, title/tagline/job relevance, 8 outcomes, 32/32 theory/reference paragraphs, 9 theory code/output blocks, 9 callouts, 3 figures, Theory playground, 8 I Do, 24 We Do, You Do, self-check, authenticated exam bank, CP-N4-A public/canonical brief+rubric and resources.

roadmap.gate: Governed Python Service Platform levanta con un comando, ejecuta tests/health checks, usa non-root y documenta configuración/recuperación

live_status.body_hydration: The public crawler does not expose a trustworthy fresh hydrated S43 body; body audit is grounded in canonical main source. No render-only defects are invented.
live_status.hours: UNRESOLVED_LIVE_SOURCE_DRIFT: public crawl says 20h; canonical main says 9h; crawl is last-month and also shows stale 1040h course total.

research_basis.use: tags are mutable; digest pins exact base; .dockerignore, multi-stage, CI build/test and cache-order guidance.

research_basis.source: Docker build cache + reproducible builds docs
research_basis.use: cache reuse is a speed mechanism, not proof that two independent builds are byte-for-byte reproducible; SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH is one reproducibility control.
short depends_on waits for running, not ready; service_healthy can wait on healthchecks; application retry is still needed for runtime failures.
prefer Compose secrets over passing sensitive values as container environment variables because env values can leak.
containers have no CPU/memory constraints by default; constraints are runtime policies and numeric budgets are workload-specific.
least privilege, capability reduction and secret management.
worked examples should fade toward independent performance; repeating the same predicate-repair grammar does not create transfer to the final artifact.
container-security background; verified still Final, so no stale-reference finding.

rejected_findings.evidence: Source explicitly documents the id as stable URL/save key; migration would be required.

rejected_findings.claim: Layer ordering deps before frequently changing app code is wrong.
rejected_findings.evidence: Docker cache documentation supports ordering less-frequently changed dependency layers before app source for cache efficiency.

rejected_findings.claim: Application retries are unnecessary when Compose supports service_healthy.
rejected_findings.evidence: service_healthy helps startup ordering; application retry is still relevant when dependencies fail/restart after startup.
Least privilege remains a legitimate container-hardening control; defect is defining it as UID>=1000 universally and failing to verify it robustly.

rejected_findings.claim: NIST SP 800-190 is obsolete and should be removed.
rejected_findings.evidence: NIST currently lists SP 800-190 Final; no superseding final publication was found.
A lab-specific resource budget is valid; defect is presenting a case budget as if it were a general safety threshold.

rejected_findings.claim: S43 must use Kubernetes instead of Compose.
rejected_findings.evidence: Roadmap explicitly scopes S43 to local containers; Kubernetes probe material is appropriate only as conceptual transfer.

findings.summary: S43 closes a capstone on top of S42 although the current S42 audit remains REPAIR_REQUIRED with P0 security evidence failures.
findings.evidence: Roadmap prereq S42; S43 opening says the S42 service can now be containerized.
findings.impact: Container packaging can legitimize an upstream service whose schema/SSRF/deletion gates are not trustworthy.
findings.fix: Require S42 critical evidence to be green before CP-N4-A closure; do not let container checks compensate for upstream security failures.

findings.summary: The final S43 project does not close the canonical CP-N4-A contract.
findings.evidence: Canonical rubric requires 200/429/401, token-redacted logs and migrations; You Do focuses Docker/Compose and never calls service.serve or verifies those API/auth/rate-limit tests.
findings.impact: A learner can complete S43 while failing required CP-N4-A behavior from S40-S42.
findings.fix: Make You Do an integrated S40-S43 gate: run the canonical seven acceptance tests plus container/recovery evidence.

findings.summary: The visible S43 rubric contradicts the canonical CP-N4-A rubric and gate rule.
findings.evidence: Visible: 25/20/15/15/15/10 percentages; canonical: correctness .35, robustness .20, maintainability .25, responsible_use .20, scale 0-3, weighted>=2.4, no critical<2, zero P0.
findings.impact: Two different evaluators can reach incompatible pass/fail decisions for the same capstone.
findings.fix: Render/use the canonical rubric in S43; remove the competing percentage rubric or explicitly derive it from the canonical source.

findings.summary: You Do readiness accepts manually flipped booleans and gate_case hardcodes outputs from a label.
findings.evidence: `readiness(bundle)` checks only `bundle.get(name) is True`; `gate_case('normal'|'breach'|...)` returns tokens without inspecting artifacts.
findings.impact: READY and breach evidence can be manufactured without Dockerfile, Compose, runbook, service or tests.
findings.fix: Read/execute artifacts and derive a signed result record from commands, exit codes and checks; booleans may summarize evidence but cannot be the evidence.

findings.summary: Roadmap says local con contenedores, but I Do/We Do are almost entirely local-Python simulations of strings/booleans and never build/run containers.
findings.evidence: Eight I Do demos and 24 We Do tasks inspect dicts/text; no docker build, compose up, inspect, exec, health request, SIGTERM, restore or scanner command is performed.
findings.impact: The learner reaches the independent container capstone without guided practice on the actual environment; outcomes are not demonstrated.
findings.fix: Use real Docker/Compose in I Do, then faded guided commands/tests in We Do, then independent one-command rebuild in You Do. Keep stdlib parsers only as preflight exercises.

findings.summary: The public CP-N4-A brief leaks pre-V3 section identities: S41 LLM finetuning, S42 graph RAG and S43 LLMOps.
findings.evidence: `public/capstones/CP-N4-A_BRIEF.md` is loaded by learner-facing CapstonesPage and contains those old names.
findings.impact: Learners see a capstone prerequisite map that contradicts the current curriculum they just completed.
findings.fix: Update public/canonical brief labels to current S40 architecture, S41 API FastAPI, S42 schemas/security, S43 containers; preserve stable IDs separately.

findings.summary: The public/canonical brief says the container is specified by Dockerfile and is not built, while S43/roadmap require a repeatable build in a new environment and one-command operation.
findings.evidence: Brief limitation: 'no se construye en el demo'; S43 callout/outcomes require build repeatible/entorno nuevo.
findings.impact: The authoritative capstone contract itself disagrees about whether the core artifact must execute.
findings.fix: Choose one contract. For current S43, require an actual local build/run/health test and revise the brief limitation accordingly.

findings.summary: T1-A calls a fabricated string comparison a stable build/dependency digest.
findings.evidence: `digest_a=f'deps:{lock_hash}'`; `digest_b` is constructed identically; equality is guaranteed by code, not measured from builds.
findings.impact: Learner can confuse a label derived from input with evidence produced by a build system.
findings.fix: Measure cache/build outputs from Docker/BuildKit or clearly call the string a conceptual cache key and never use it as gate evidence.

findings.summary: The lesson treats same lock + dependency cache reuse as evidence that a repeatable build exists.
findings.evidence: T1-A criterion and self-check use 'same logical deps digest'; Docker docs distinguish cache reuse from reproducible build controls.
findings.impact: A fast cached rebuild can pass while fresh builds differ because of base images, package indexes, timestamps or other inputs.
findings.fix: Separate objectives: cache efficiency vs reproducible fresh build. Add clean/no-cache build comparison and pin all declared inputs; optionally teach SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH as an advanced reproducibility control.

findings.summary: Multiple learner-facing Dockerfile fixtures use `@sha256:demo`, which is not a valid image digest.
findings.evidence: T1-A and T1-B We Do GOOD_DF use the placeholder; exact-digest theory later says short/fake digests must fail.
findings.impact: The supposedly transferable Dockerfile cannot be built and directly conflicts with the section's own digest validation mental model.
findings.fix: Use a deterministic fixture image reference valid for the test environment or an explicit `<64-hex-demo-digest>` token that is never presented as runnable; preferably build from a local fixture image/digest.

findings.summary: You Do explicitly accepts 'digest o tag no latest' although Docker documents tags as mutable and S43 theory requires digest for exact bytes.
findings.evidence: You Do requirement versus T1-B exact DIGEST regex/T4-A discussion and Docker build best practices.
findings.impact: A mutable base can pass the final reproducibility gate.
findings.fix: Require digest pin for the graded reproducibility path; teach controlled update automation separately.

findings.summary: The lesson equates non-root with UID >=1000.
findings.evidence: Outcome/T1-B repeatedly define application UID >=1000 as non-root.
findings.impact: Learner can infer that UID 1-999 is root or that 1000 itself proves least privilege; neither is generally true.
findings.fix: State: UID 0 is root; this lab adopts >=1000 as a course policy to avoid system/service UIDs. Verify the actual runtime user and privileges.

findings.summary: T1-B E3 rejects valid named non-root users and accepts malformed digest references.
findings.evidence: `_user_uid` only understands digits/root; `pinned='@sha256:' in dockerfile` accepts `sha256:abc`.
findings.impact: Reference solution produces both false negatives and false positives on a security gate.
findings.fix: Inspect built image/container user (`docker inspect`/id) and parse exact digest; do not infer runtime identity from a two-case text parser.

findings.summary: Runtime size predicates allow nonsensical negative values and nonpositive budgets.
findings.evidence: `slim_ok = runtime_mb <= max_mb` without domain checks.
findings.impact: Invalid measurements can create PASS and teach incomplete validation.
findings.fix: Require finite positive runtime_mb and positive max_mb before budget comparison; get actual image size from Docker rather than a supplied integer in final evidence.

findings.summary: The prose groups slim and distroless as if both necessarily remove the shell.
findings.evidence: 'Distroless/slim recortan shell y paquetes'.
findings.impact: Learner may expect Python slim to behave like distroless during debugging/security review.
findings.fix: Separate the cases: slim reduces packages but may retain shell/tools; distroless intentionally omits many conventional userland tools.

findings.summary: The outcome promises no extra capabilities, but the final project never verifies container capabilities.
findings.evidence: T1-B theory uses a supplied `caps` set; You Do requirements/readiness have no capability artifact or command.
findings.impact: A privileged/cap-add container can satisfy the final four booleans.
findings.fix: Add runtime inspection/test for granted capabilities and define the course policy as 'no additional capabilities unless justified', rather than `not caps` as an abstract set.

findings.summary: Secret leakage detection searches only the substrings SECRET= and PASSWORD=.
findings.evidence: T2-A theory/I Do/We Do scanners ignore TOKEN, API_KEY, ARG/RUN secrets, copied .env, command history and arbitrary secret names.
findings.impact: Images with embedded credentials can pass the lesson's security gate.
findings.fix: Teach build-context exclusion and real secret scanning/history inspection with synthetic seeded tokens; pattern lists are demonstration aids, not proof.

findings.summary: `runtime_only` is inferred solely from not detecting a baked secret.
findings.evidence: `runtime_only: not baked`.
findings.impact: No secret at all and a correctly injected runtime secret are treated as the same evidence.
findings.fix: Verify the service receives the secret at runtime from the declared secret mechanism while image/history remains clean; test rotation without rebuild.

findings.summary: The lesson lists orchestrator environment variables as a normal secret-injection mechanism without explaining the leakage risk or preferring Compose secrets.
findings.evidence: T2-A prose; current Docker docs explicitly recommend secrets rather than sensitive container environment variables.
findings.impact: A security section can normalize a weaker pattern exactly where a safer Compose mechanism is in scope.
findings.fix: Prefer Compose/runtime secret mounts; mention host env only as a source for a Compose secret or a constrained platform-specific fallback with explicit risk.

findings.summary: S43 warns against copying .env/secrets but never teaches `.dockerignore` or build-context minimization.
findings.evidence: No `.dockerignore` artifact appears in outcomes/You Do; Docker's current lab and best-practices guide use it to keep `.env`/irrelevant files out of build context.
findings.impact: Learner can follow the lesson and still send secrets into build context or accidentally COPY them later.
findings.fix: Require `.dockerignore` with synthetic secret/context regression test.

findings.summary: T2-B claims readiness and SIGTERM are tested, but code accepts booleans like `drains=True` and never sends a signal or calls a health endpoint.
findings.evidence: `health_status(ready,live)` and `on_sigterm(drains,grace)` are pure proxies.
findings.impact: A process that ignores SIGTERM or always returns 200 can pass if the fixture says otherwise.
findings.fix: Run container; curl readiness with dependency healthy/unhealthy, create in-flight work, send docker stop/SIGTERM and assert drain/exit within configured grace.

findings.summary: `grace >=20` is presented as the definition of graceful shutdown.
findings.evidence: T2-B code and exercises hardcode >=20 seconds.
findings.impact: Learner may optimize to a magic number rather than a workload-specific termination budget; Docker's stop timeout is configurable.
findings.fix: Define a lab `termination_grace_seconds` configuration and require observed drain <= configured budget; explain 20/30 seconds as examples, not universal thresholds.

findings.summary: T3-A says Compose declares healthchecks per service, but MINI_COMPOSE has no `healthcheck:` and health is a supplied set.
findings.evidence: MINI_COMPOSE services only contain networks/depends_on/retry env; `healthy` set drives PASS.
findings.impact: The exemplar teaches that writing `healthy={'api',...}` is equivalent to a service healthcheck.
findings.fix: Use actual healthcheck definitions and `docker compose up --wait`/inspect; include `depends_on.condition: service_healthy` where startup readiness matters.

findings.summary: A `DB_MAX_ATTEMPTS` environment token/boolean is treated as proof of application retry/backoff.
findings.evidence: T3-A contract requires token of retries; stack_ok receives `retries=True`.
findings.impact: Configuration can exist while application ignores it or retries incorrectly.
findings.fix: Exercise dependency restart/failure and assert bounded retry/backoff from real service logs/behavior.

findings.summary: front/back networks are made a universal PASS condition without tying the requirement to actual exposed ports/trust boundaries.
findings.evidence: T3-A `NETS <= networks` hard gate.
findings.impact: Learner memorizes topology names instead of least-exposure reasoning; equivalent secure compositions can false-fail.
findings.fix: Grade the security property: DB/cache not publicly exposed and service communication matches the threat model. front/back is one implementation pattern.

findings.summary: Theory teaches expand then later contract, but code/We Do allow only `migration == 'expand'` and classify contract as rollback.
findings.evidence: migration_gate and T3-B exercises.
findings.impact: Learner cannot model the second half of the migration strategy and may infer contract is always unsafe.
findings.fix: Represent phases: expand while old code exists; deploy compatible code; only then contract when no reader needs old schema; test both valid and invalid contract transitions.

findings.summary: `migrate_before_api=True`, `old_ok`, `ephemeral_reset` and `backup_restored` are declared flags rather than executed migration/recovery evidence.
findings.evidence: T3-B code and reference exercises.
findings.impact: A critical CP-N4-A failure 'Sin migraciones' can be masked by booleans.
findings.fix: Run a small real DB migration and restore fixture, record command/exit/schema state before/after, and gate API startup on migration success.

findings.summary: T4-A theory explicitly rejects short fake digests, but I Do and We Do approve `sha256:abc` using `startswith('sha256:')`.
findings.evidence: Theory uses exact `^sha256:[0-9a-f]{64}$`; I Do calls `stages(...,'sha256:abc')` and prints pinned; We Do solutions repeat prefix test.
findings.impact: The reference practice trains the learner to pass the exact invalid value the theory warned against; supply-chain/reproducibility gate false-greens.
findings.fix: Reuse the exact digest validator everywhere and couple the digest to a real lock/artifact; add short/malformed digest regression tests.

findings.summary: A string that looks like a digest is allowed to stand in for a dependency lock without proving what file it hashes or whether installation enforces it.
findings.evidence: T4-A I Do/We Do records `lock_hash` separately; final requirements do not verify lock content/`--require-hashes` execution.
findings.impact: Learner can hash arbitrary text and claim reproducible dependencies.
findings.fix: Hash the actual lock file, verify the hash in the evidence manifest, and execute package installation with that lock/hash policy.

findings.summary: Runtime toolchain detection is a substring search for gcc/g++.
findings.evidence: T4-A multistage parser.
findings.impact: clang, make, rustc, build-essential or comments can evade/trigger the rule; the construct is 'minimal runtime', not two words.
findings.fix: Inspect installed packages/files or assert explicit runtime allowlist/base; use substring parsing only as a toy preflight.

findings.summary: Theory permits signed CVE exceptions, but every executable gate requires critical==0 and has no exception record/expiry/owner.
findings.evidence: T4-B p1 vs scan_gate and We Do.
findings.impact: The written policy and automated policy disagree; learners cannot implement governed exceptions.
findings.fix: Either remove the exception claim from S43 or model a versioned exception with vulnerability ID, rationale, owner, expiry and compensating control.

findings.summary: The scan gate trusts a critical-CVE count detached from image digest, scanner version and vulnerability database timestamp.
findings.evidence: T4-B inputs are `critical: int` and text `CRITICAL: 0`.
findings.impact: A stale or unrelated scan can approve a different image.
findings.fix: Persist image digest + scanner/tool version + DB timestamp + report hash; gate the exact built artifact.

findings.summary: 512 MiB and 1 CPU are treated as the valid upper range without consistently labeling them as CASO-TRU-043 lab budgets.
findings.evidence: T4-B predicate `0 < mem <=512` and `0 < cpu <=1.0`.
findings.impact: Learner may infer these numbers are container best practices rather than a workload budget.
findings.fix: Declare `LAB_MEMORY_BUDGET_MB=512`/`LAB_CPU_BUDGET=1.0` and explain that production budgets come from workload/SLO/capacity evidence.

findings.summary: Tagline/roadmap demand one-command operation and a repeatable build in a new environment, but You Do starter only names file paths and prints status tokens.
findings.evidence: ARTIFACTS contains names; no subprocess/command/test opens those files or starts the stack.
findings.impact: The central learner-facing promise is not assessed.
findings.fix: Provide a real acceptance command such as `make verify`/script that builds, starts, waits for health, runs canonical tests, stops, cleans, and emits an evidence manifest.

findings.summary: Visible rubric grades SLO, observability and lineage even though S43's final starter neither produces nor teaches those artifacts as assessed constructs.
findings.evidence: 15% 'Operación: SLO, observabilidad y rollback'; roadmap places CI/CD/supply-chain in S44 and later production observability elsewhere.
findings.impact: Learner is graded on hidden/future requirements while canonical rubric already defines a different contract.
findings.fix: Use canonical CP-N4-A rubric; keep S43-specific operational evidence inside its defined acceptance tests.

findings.summary: The learner-facing Theory playground for legacy id `llmops` still teaches LLMOps tracing, RAG, RAGAS metrics and token cost instead of S43 containers.
findings.evidence: SectionView maps `'llmops'` to `Practica tracing y eval (simulado)` with retriever/generator/RAGAS/cost tracking.
findings.impact: A complete unrelated conceptual graph appears inside the container lesson, increasing interference and reviving the obsolete pre-V3 topic.
findings.fix: Keep stable id `llmops` but replace the playground mapping with an on-topic Docker/Compose/reproducibility simulation or disable it for S43.

findings.summary: Self-check Q1 calls the fabricated logical deps digest sufficient evidence; Q3 defines CP-N4-A only as container build/non-root/limits/shutdown.
findings.evidence: Current five self-check questions.
findings.impact: Retrieval practice strengthens two curriculum defects instead of detecting them.
findings.fix: Replace Q1 with actual fresh-build/cache evidence distinction; make CP-N4-A question include canonical API/auth/rate/log/migration acceptance plus container criticals.

findings.summary: Five recognition questions cannot sample the eight outcomes or integrated capstone gate; migration, lock validation, scan provenance and real restore are largely absent.
findings.evidence: Self-check covers cache, health/root response, gate summary, secrets, cache ordering.
findings.impact: Learner can pass recall while missing the riskiest operational contracts.
findings.fix: Use at least one scenario per critical gate and integrated troubleshooting decisions; keep recognition only as retrieval warm-up.

findings.summary: The seeded S43 bank has broad concept coverage but mostly asks declarative multiple-choice facts rather than interpreting concrete Docker/Compose/scan/migration artifacts.
findings.evidence: Examples: COPY requirements cache benefit, multi-stage definition, lockfiles, CVE scan, non-root purpose.
findings.impact: The authenticated exam does not independently verify the portfolio skills it gates.
findings.fix: Keep concept variants but make them artifact-based: Dockerfile diff, Compose health condition, migration runbook, scan report and resource config.

findings.summary: Roadmap requires >=70% plus 100% critical items, but platform scoring has no `critical` field and passes solely on total >=70.
findings.evidence: `QuestionKey` lacks critical; `passed: clamped >= PASS_THRESHOLD`.
findings.impact: A learner can miss root/secrets/migration/health security questions and compensate with easy cache questions.
findings.fix: Add critical metadata and require all critical answers correct in addition to total threshold.

findings.summary: The 24 We Do tasks repeat E1 inverted-predicate repair, E2 valid/adversarial/missing, E3 text parser/token routing.
findings.evidence: Pattern repeated across all 8 subtopics.
findings.impact: The learner can master task grammar without learning Docker commands, runtime inspection or recovery procedure; guidance is not faded toward authentic performance.
findings.fix: Alternate worked real commands, completion tasks, debugging, prediction, failure injection and independent container verification; return to a worked example only when a genuinely new operation is introduced.

findings.summary: Advanced terms accumulate faster than their operational relationships are demonstrated: digest, capabilities, distroless, build context, restore drill, OOM, CVE, expand/contract, builder/runtime.
findings.evidence: Several are named/briefly glossed but never tied to a real command/artifact before repeated exercise tokens.
findings.impact: Learners may memorize labels without a trigger→artifact→command→observable-result model.
findings.fix: Introduce each term with Spanish-first mechanism and one real observable command before abbreviating it later.

findings.summary: The resource list mixes strong primary Docker/NIST/OWASP references with generic or beginner Python course links and omits direct links for controls the section currently gets wrong.
findings.evidence: Coursera generic Docker search, MIT 6.100L, CS50P, Py4E; no direct Compose secrets/startup-order/resource constraints/reproducible-build/.dockerignore resources.
findings.impact: Learners are sent to broad beginner material instead of the exact authoritative docs needed to repair the section's hardest misconceptions.
findings.fix: Prioritize Docker secrets, startup order/service_healthy, resource constraints, build cache/reproducible builds, `.dockerignore`, USER/capability hardening and scan provenance; demote generic Python courses.

USABLE: Dockerfile/image/container distinction as a starting mental model
dependency layers before frequently changing source for cache efficiency
digest pinning is stronger than mutable tags
readiness and liveness are different questions
depends_on does not eliminate the need for application resilience
resource limits should not be absent/unbounded
runtime secrets should not be baked into image layers
MISCONCEPTION_RISK: same lock + fake logical digest proves reproducible build
UID>=1000 is the definition of non-root
absence of SECRET=/PASSWORD= proves runtime-only secrets
critical=0 text proves the built image is clean
CP-N4-A is only a container gate
legacy llmops playground content still belongs in S43
